name: Bike Transportation
short: Crated two-wheeler transport that can ride along with your household consignment.
description: Bikes and scooters move as crated cargo: drained to safe fuel levels, mirrors and levers padded, bodywork wrapped, and the whole machine secured in a wooden or reinforced crate. On intercity moves the crate can travel with your household consignment — one coordinator, one delivery window, one bill.

features.title: Proper crating
features.text: Bodywork wrapped, levers and mirrors padded, and the bike secured in a crate — not lashed loose between furniture.

features.title: Condition documentation
features.text: Photographed condition report at pickup, matched again at delivery, so any transit marks are objectively attributable.

features.title: Rides with your household move
features.text: The crate can share the truck with your household goods on intercity corridors, saving a separate shipment.

features.title: Door-to-door
features.text: Pickup from your address and delivery to the new one, including society gate formalities at both ends.

faqs.q: How is a bike packed for intercity transport?
faqs.a: Fuel is brought to a safe level, mirrors/levers are padded, the body is wrapped, and the bike is secured inside a wooden or reinforced crate. The crate rides with the household consignment or as standalone cargo.

faqs.q: What does bike transport typically cost?
faqs.a: It depends on your inventory, floors, lift access, packing level and distance. We run a free survey (video or doorstep) and then confirm an itemised written quote — no advance is needed to book.

faqs.q: Do I need to empty the fuel tank?
faqs.a: Not fully — keep it around a quarter tank or less, which is the safe-transport convention for crated vehicles. We'll confirm at pickup; the condition report notes the fuel level.

faqs.q: Which documents are needed for bike transport?
faqs.a: RC copy and owner ID at pickup; interstate consignment documentation is handled by us. The owner or an authorised person countersigns the condition report at both ends.
